stem: Based on a random sample, 38% of a population is estimated to have a certain trait, with a margin of error of 4 percentage points. Which of the following statements is best supported by the data?

choices.A: Less than 35% of the population has the trait.
choices.B: More than 30% of the population has the trait.
choices.C: More than 40% of the population has the trait.
choices.D: Exactly 38% of the population has the trait.

solution: Plausible values for the population percent: \(38 - 4 = 34\%\) to \(38 + 4 = 42\%\).
Every plausible value is greater than 30%, so the statement that more than 30% of the population has the trait is supported.
The other statements are contradicted by some plausible values in the range.

explanation.A: Incorrect. Plausible values go up to 42%, so it is not shown that the percent is less than 35%.
explanation.B: Correct. The plausible values run from 34% to 42%, and all of them are greater than 30%.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Plausible values from 34% to 40% are not greater than 40%, so this is not supported.
explanation.D: Incorrect. 38% is an estimate; the margin of error shows the population percent is not known exactly.

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'D': 'A', 'A': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'C': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'D', 'B': 'A', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'C'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
lo, hi = 38 - 4, 38 + 4
assert lo > 30 and not lo > 40 and not hi < 35
assert answer == 'A' and 'More than 30%' in choices['A']
